name: Solarworld Energy Solutions Ltd
title: Solarworld Energy Solutions Ltd - 544532 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 235% YoY to INR591 crore, but EBITDA margin was 12.1% and FY26 PAT margin 8.5%, below the 11% promised earlier.
summary.overview: Solarworld reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR591 crore (up 235% YoY), EBITDA of INR73 crore (12.1% margin) and PAT of INR49 crore (8.1% net margin). For FY26, total income was INR1,416 crore (up 1.57% YoY), EBITDA INR187.9 crore (13.3%) and PAT INR120.4 crore (8.5%). Management blamed a loss-making initial module ramp after ALMM approval in December 2025 and sharp raw material cost increases in Q4 linked to the West Asia conflict. The company is pivoting toward BESS, with a 582 MWac / 1.2 GWh DC BESS project pipeline and a 3.4 GW BESS line in trials.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: FY26 EPC revenue about INR1,250 crore; management cites EPC PAT margin close to 10.5%. EPC margin guided at 9-11% through the cycle and 8-11% overall for FY27. Solar EPC order book about INR1,674 crore.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: FY26 BESS revenue was nil; management guides INR800-1,000 crore in FY27. BESS order book about INR1,136 crore. Q4 orders from NTPC at Solapur and Unchahar aggregate about 514 MWh, order value about INR5 billion incl. O&M. BESS margin guided at 14-15% PBT.

segments.name: Solar module manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.5 GW Roorkee module line began operations after ALMM approval in December 2025; about two to two-and-a-half months of run-time in FY26 produced a slight loss. Breakeven at about 30-35% utilisation; FY26-27 utilisation expected at 40-45% on about 600 MW captive NTPC REL orders, rising to 60-65% with more orders. Line capex about INR146 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order book conversion target at least 70% of about INR2,800 crore, i.e. about INR2,000 crore revenue; EPC about INR2,000 crore including BESS INR800-1,000 crore.
Management expects 40-45% revenue growth in FY27 and says it will not sustain FY26's 200-250% growth.
Overall EBITDA/PAT margin guided at 8-11%; sustaining current margins if the West Asia conflict eases, with slight downside if raw material prices keep rising.
BESS margin guided at 14-15% PBT; 3.4 GW BESS line capex about INR55-60 crore, potential revenue about INR3,000 crore at full capacity (740 containers at INR4.5 crore each).
Q1 and Q2 seasonally weak; Q3 and Q4 strong. Management declined to give a half-yearly split.
1.2 GW solar cell line at Pandhurna targeted for commercial operation by June 2027; cell-line funds to be deployed from Q3 FY27.
No near-term plans to add module or cell capacity until about 75-80% captive utilisation is visible.
capex_capacity: Module: 1.5 GW Roorkee facility (7.5 acres, automated ATW and Horad lines) operational; output 600-750 W TOPCon-type panels across M10R, G12R and G12 configurations.
BESS: 3.4 GW fully automated line (KUKA robotics) ready, trials underway; capex about INR55-60 crore already spent.
Solar cell: 1.2 GW line at Pandhurna, approvals mostly received, construction to start around June 2026, commercial operation targeted by June 2027.
Junction box: 5 GW line being set up in a joint venture; site ready for trials.

Operational capacity to be added on commissioning: a 272 MW project and a 70 MW project expected to complete in June 2026; management expects about 600 MW near term, about 700 MW next quarter and about 1.5 GW by year-end.
demand_pricing: PSU tenders were about 40 GW last year; the company executes about 1-1.5 GW a year, so it sees limited impact from a slower tendering market.
Raw material costs up sharply since Oct 2025: copper about +40%, aluminium about +50%, steel higher; INR depreciated from about 85-86 to about 96 per USD, affecting BESS imported inputs.
ALMM List-II (cells) applies from June 2026; management expects 90-95% of projects to shift to DCR cells, with a possible 6-12 month cell shortage.
Current order book has no ALMM-2 cell requirement, giving a headway of about a year. Lithium cells for BESS are sourced from China as no Indian supplier exists.
PPA signing delays after L1 bids and grid connectivity constraints are slowing the solar tender market; management expects connectivity to take 10-12 more months to resolve.
Claims filed with SJVN for about INR219 crore; only INR52 crore recognised as receivable. Ind AS allows recognition only after dispute-board award.

qa_highlights.question: PAT margin is 8-8.5% versus the 11% promised earlier, and top line is short of the INR1,500 crore target. What is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPC PAT margin is about 10.5%, with the module loss from a short ramp and Q4 raw material headwinds dragging the total. Guidance is INR1,900-2,000 crore revenue and 8-11% overall margins.

qa_highlights.question: Battery cell unit timeline, and when will it contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: The 1.2 GW cell line at Pandhurna is now targeted for commercial start by June 2027, with construction starting around June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expense rise, and what is the BESS capex and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expense rose to INR83 million from INR74 million; last year's base included a INR140 million write-off that was recovered this year. The 3.4 GW BESS line capex is INR55-60 crore; margin 14-15% PBT.

qa_highlights.question: How will the module line utilisation ramp, and what is breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven is around 30-35% utilisation. Utilisation should reach 40-45% on existing NTPC REL orders (about 600 MW), rising to 60-65% with new orders. All existing EPC orders can be serviced in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand module or cell capacity, and why are PPAs being rescinded?
qa_highlights.answer: No expansion planned until 75-80% captive use is visible. PPA delays stem from DISCOM absorption and transmission constraints; management expects resolution by around end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ROW, labour and the EPC tender pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: ROW compensation is moving to market rates, which helps, but management does not see it as the biggest hurdle; no major labour issues. Tender activity is slower, but the company's order book is full.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from copper, aluminium, steel and INR depreciation; management guides 8-11% overall margin range.
Execution risk on the 60-40 BESS to EPC mix, with BESS revenue ramp from nil to INR800-1,000 crore and most BESS projects due by June 2027.
Timing of the 1.2 GW solar cell line (June 2027) and its funding deployment from Q3 FY27.
Cell shortage under ALMM-2 for 6-12 months could delay projects, though the company's own orders are insulated for about a year.
SJVN claim recovery (INR219 crore filed vs INR52 crore booked) is uncertain and timing unknown.
Customer concentration in PSU and NTPC REL orders; PPA rescissions and slower PSU tendering.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategy and BESS growth, but defensive on margins and the earlier 11% PAT commitment. Management gave specific, number-heavy answers on capacity and revenue but was vague on quarterly phasing, order inflow and pricing outcomes.
key_quotes: So we would say somewhere between 8% to 11% is where we should lie in terms of overall margins.
We expect to grow by around 40%-45% this year as well.
So maybe end of this year is when most of the demand should start coming in.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 40-45% (~INR2,000 crore from a INR2,800 crore order book at 70% conversion), backed by a INR1,674 crore solar EPC and INR1,136 crore BESS order book, NTPC captive orders of ~600 MW, and new capacity (1.5 GW modules operational, 3.4 GW BESS line in trials), though margin guidance was cut to 8-11% and management said FY26's 200-250% growth will not be sustained.
